title: Reid Ducharme standing out in Siena men's basketball team's summer workouts - NewsBreak
text:
By ​Tommy Valentine ,
1 hours ago
LOUDONVILLE, N.Y. ( NEWS10 ) — Last week, NEWS10 Sports caught up with the Siena men’s basketball team amid summer workouts, and first-year head coach Nevada Smith was sure to point out one player who’s really caught his attention.
Redshirt junior guard Reid Ducharme is coming off a season where he didn’t appear in a single game; dealing with a left shoulder injury that later required surgery.
But Ducharme is back, healthy, and Smith has lofty expectations for the former four-star recruit and Xavier University transfer, who’s entering year three with the program.
“Reid has probably had the best spring, summer; he’s been terrific,” said Smith. “I think he has a chance to be a guy that could lead the Metro [Conference] in scoring. He can really shoot. He can really score. His body looks great; he’s healthy. He’s been really, really high-level since we’ve been back.”
Ducharme only averaged 4.6 points per game in 25 games during the 2024-25 campaign – his first at Siena. After failing to see the court last season, Smith believes Ducharme has a chip on his shoulder entering this season.
“I think he’s come in with a purpose. He’s decided that people haven’t seen the real Reid Ducharme play since he’s been at Siena. I don’t forget…he was at [Brewster Academy] and a top 100 player and everyone in the country wanted him. He’s still that guy. He just hasn’t been able to do it here, and I think he has the avenue this year to be able to do it. The way we play really fits him and the way he shoots the ball is just different than most people. He’s an elite shooter. He’s not okay; he’s not good; he’s elite. He’s one of the best in the country. I’d be shocked if he didn’t shoot 40%. And that’s what we want from him every day.”
That high praise from Smith only stokes the fire within Ducharme.
“If you want one person to have confidence in you, it’s your head coach,” said Ducharme. “Just knowing that he has my back makes me want to work harder, get in the gym more, not let him down, but also not let my team down, ’cause they know what I’m capable of doing.”
While the talk of scoring averages and three-point percentages is great, Ducharme said his primary goal this season is helping lead Siena to a second straight Metro Conference championship in whatever capacity he can.
